gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the UGREEN HD151 passive 48 Gbps extension has a fixed 3 m (9.8 ft) total run at 8K60/4K240. With the 1 m extension, the male cable can be at most 2 m. With the 2 m (6.6 ft) extension, it can be at most 1 m. Buying the longer extension adds no reach. It only moves the 3 m between the two cables.
standout_why: I read four ChatGPT results. The cited Cable Matters page gives only the active cable's own 6.6 ft size and a vague line saying it can extend an 8K run by 16.4 ft. The cited iTechGuides guide says there is 'no universal maximum HDMI cable length' and gives no combined cable-plus-extension limit for 48 Gbps. Shinforce (rank 8) has only rough guidance like '10 feet is the longest run you want from a passive HDMI 2.1 cable'. Bespokecable (rank 12) gives a combined limit only for 4K passive (about 25 ft / 7.5 m) and none for 48 Gbps or 8K. I also read Revactic's female-to-male list (rank 2 in the second chat). It includes the UGREEN 3.3 ft extension but gives no connected-cable limit, only 'evaluate the complete run'. ChatGPT's own answer warned that the cable plus the extension can be 'too long' but gave no number. I couldn't read the cited bestways.com HD151 page (HTTP 429 three times). It is a reseller listing and might copy UGREEN's length note, so I scored 2, not 3.
decides: This confirms and sharpens the split between short and long runs. The UGREEN HD151 is the pick only if your existing cable plus the extension totals 3 m (9.8 ft) or less. A 1 m extension plus a cable of 2 m or less works, and so does a 2 m extension plus a cable of 1 m or less. A common 2 m TV cable plus the 2 m extension is 4 m, which is 1 m over the limit, so 4K120/8K may drop out. Past about 10 ft total, the shopper should go to the powered Cable Matters active extension, or skip extensions and use one long active/optical cable or an HDBaseT kit.

findings.label: Can a male-to-female extension be HDMI-certified?
findings.value: HDMI.org's certification page lists only Ultra96 and Ultra High Speed HDMI cables as certified, and those must pass testing at an ATC (HDMI's authorized test center) and carry a label. It does not mention extension cables at all.
findings.source_title: Ultra High Speed HDMI Cable – HDMI.org
findings.note: Neither candidate claims an HDMI certification label on the pages I read. This backs up ChatGPT's point that one certified cable is the safer choice for long runs.
